findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh logger, discarding recorded log calls
findings.body: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()` instead of the receiver, so anything logged through `FromContext` is recorded on a discarded logger and is invisible to a test holding the original `*TestLogger`. Because `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` was changed to `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info("Plugin Request Completed", ...)`, a test that injects a `*TestLogger` and asserts on `logger.InfoLogs.Calls`/`Message` will now observe zero calls, and the middleware's log output can no longer be asserted on the injected logger at all. The fake should return the receiver (or share the `Logs` state) so callers can inspect what was logged; otherwise this double silently hides regressions in the newly refactored logging path.

findings.title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware and infra FromContext have no tests
findings.body: The entire refactor now depends on the new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware`/`instrumentContext` to reproduce the log fields that `LoggerMiddleware` used to add explicitly (endpoint, pluginId, and the conditional dsName/dsUID when `DataSourceInstanceSettings` is set and uname when `User` is set), plus the new `grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext` in pkg/plugins/log/logger.go (including its `*log.ConcreteLogger` type assertion and `!ok` fallback). None of these are covered by tests; the only test change in the PR is a one-line rename in metrics_middleware_test.go. A regression here (e.g. attributes not being applied or the type assertion failing) would silently drop pluginId/endpoint/uname/dsName/dsUID/traceID from the "Plugin Request Completed" log without any failing test. Add tests asserting the produced contextual attributes.

findings.title: FromContext fallback silently drops traceID and all contextual attributes
findings.body: `grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext` type-asserts `d.l.FromContext(ctx)` to `*log.ConcreteLogger` and, on failure, returns `d.New()`. `d.New()` is a base logger with no traceID and no contextual attributes, so if the infra logger ever returns a different implementation (e.g. a context-aware wrapper type), every request-completed log emitted via `LoggerMiddleware` would silently lose pluginId/endpoint/uname/dsName/dsUID/traceID with no error or fallback signal. The fallback masks the failure rather than degrading gracefully. Storing the infra `log.Logger` interface (which exposes Debug/Info/etc.) instead of `*log.ConcreteLogger` would avoid the assertion entirely.

findings.title: Adding FromContext to the Logger interface is a breaking change for implementers
findings.body: Adding the `FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger` method to the exported `plugins/log.Logger` interface breaks every implementation. This PR only updates `grafanaInfraLogWrapper` and `TestLogger`. Verify there are no other implementations (in particular generated mocks, e.g. via mockery, or test doubles in other packages) that now fail to satisfy the interface and break the build; if any exist they must be regenerated/updated in this PR.

findings.title: Test function still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware after rename
findings.body: The file and middleware were renamed from Instrumentation to Metrics, but the test function is still `TestInstrumentationMiddleware`. This is a leftover from an incomplete rename and is misleading now that `InstrumentationMiddleware` no longer exists. Rename it to `TestMetricsMiddleware` for consistency.
